newsitem.title: ITALY: Pension reform Italy's last chance for EMU - IMF.
newsitem.headline: Pension reform Italy's last chance for EMU - IMF.

text.p: Crucial pension reform counts as Italy's last chance to make the grade for early EMU entry, an International Monetary Fund (IMF) official was quoted as saying in an interview with Panorama weekly news magazine.

"Action is needed on the anomalies of the social welfare system, and particularly on length of service pensions, so that structural cuts are defined, approved and implemented by the latest along with the budget for 1998," said Massimo Russo, special adviser to IMF managing director Michel Camdessus.
The budget for next year should by law go before parliament by the end of September and be approved by both houses by end-December.
"If Italy had implemented 20 trillion lire worth of structural measures in March then supplementary corrective budgetary meaures would not have been necessary," Russo said.

Prime Minister Romano Prodi's centre-left government has recently passed a controversial mini-budget aimed at trimming the 1997 deficit by 15.5 trillion lire, seen vital to Italy's drive to join Europe's single currency.
This brings to nearly 100 trillion lire the total of belt-tightening measures introduced in the past year to whip Italy's economy into shape for early EMU entry.
Russo said that apart from action on pensions there was little room for other public spending cuts.
